lawyer:
Mohammad Ozair Farooq, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mohammad Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
AKM Nazrul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record  ------ For Respondent No.1 
Not represented ------ Respondent No.2.

Nasima Akhter  ------ Petitioner

full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Haque J: This petition for leave to appeal at the instance of the defendant-petitioner is directed against the Judgment and order dated 21-1-2002 passed by the Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 122 of 1992 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 24-3-1992, passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit, No. 40 of 1991 dismissing the suit. 

 2. The present respondent No.1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 30 of 1989 in the Court of Subordinate Judge Narayanganj against the defendant petitioner and another praying for a decree of Specific Performance of Contract stating, inter alia, that the defendant No.1 (hereinafter referred to as petitioner) was the owner of the suit property described in the schedule of the plaint on the basis of the registered deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz No. 40287 dated 15-12-1980 and also by inheritance. The defendant No.1 petitioner offered to sell the suit property to the plaintiff, consideration of the suit property was fixed at Taka 1,68,000. The defendant No.1 on 4-3-1988 executed a Bainanama upon receiving Taka 5,000 and handed over possession of the suit property to the plaintiff. 

 6. The defendant No.1 neither submitted any written statement nor contested the suit. The plaintiff examined two witnesses. The learned Subordinate Judge after considering the evidence on record and hearing the parties by its judgment and decree dated 24-3-1992 dismissed the suit. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 24-3-1992 the plaintiff as appellant filed First Appeal No. 122-of 1992 in the High Court Division. 

 9. First Appeal was heard by the Division Bench of the High Court Division who by their judgment and decree dated 21-1-2002 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. The High Court Division decreed the suit for Specific Performance of Contract in favour of the plaintiff appellant and directed the plaintiff to pay Taka 4 (four) lac to the defendant No.1 as solarium and get the sale deed executed and registered. 

 10. The defendant No.1 being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division has come up with this petition for leave to appeal. 

 11. Mr Md Ozair Farooq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioner, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in decreeing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract in spite of its positive findings that the plaintiff has failed to prove tender and/or payment of balance consideration money of Taka 1,63,000 and, as such, the judgment and decree of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate submits that the positive findings of the High Court Division is that there is no other independent witness to support tender of balance consideration money not to speak of payment of balance consideration money. Yet the High Court Division allowed the appeal and set aside the Judgment and decree passed by the trial court. The learned Advocate submits that the High Court Division ought not to have decreed the suit because the plaintiff did not come to Court with clean hands  and his pleadings and depositions in Court are self- contradictory. The learned Advocate further submits that the High Court Division failed to take into consideration that the plaintiff failed to prove the bainanama in accordance with law and, as such, the impugned Judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. The High Court Division has held that PW 2, the scribe, duly proved bainanama and so the learned Subordinate Judge acted illegally in holding that the bainanama has not been duly proved. 

 12. It appears that the defendant No.1 neither submitted any written statement nor contested the suit. Therefore, the defendant No.1 did not deny the existence of bainanama between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1. Moreover, it appears that the scribe of bainanama has proved the same. Therefore, the High Court Division has rightly held that the bainanama has been duly proved and this is the foundation upon which the High Court Division has decreed the suit for Specific Performance of Contract. 

 16. Be that as it may, it has been proved that there was an agreement for sale of the suit land for an amount of Taka 1,68,000 between the parties and at the time of baina only Taka 5,000 was paid. Accordingly, the High Court Division has decreed the suit by providing solatium which the plaintiff agreed to pay to the defendant No.1.
